answer: The fix is the `except Http404:` clause in `get_caller()` (django/views/debug.py), which `technical_404_response` calls for `raising_view_name`. A path converter's `to_python` raising Http404 escapes `RoutePattern.match` (which only catches ValueError) and `URLResolver.resolve` (which only catches Resolver404), so `response_for_exception` calls `technical_404_response` while `request.resolver_match` is still None. `get_caller` then calls `resolve(request.path)` again, and the converter raises Http404 a second time. Catching only Resolver404 there would let that exception escape the debug view, and runserver would show "A server error occurred". Catching Http404 at line 103 (`except Http404: pass`) lets the technical 404 response render. I did not check the 404 template or handler code, so the template rendering with `urlpatterns=None` is assumed.

The inner query's select/GROUP BY gets clobbered in Exact.get_prep_lookup (django/db/models/lookups.py). When the filter value is a sliced Query (has_limit_one), the Exact lookup rewrites the subquery's select to just the pk (clear_select_clause() + add_fields(["pk"])), replacing the values('m')/annotation select with U0.id, so the compiler groups by the pk (GROUP BY U0."id") instead of the original GROUP BY email. The fix is the guard `if not self.rhs.has_select_fields:`. It limits the pk rewrite to subqueries that have no explicit select fields. A values()-built query has has_select_fields=True (set in Query.set_values), so it keeps its own select and GROUP BY. The `In` lookup has the same guard at lookups.py:462.

MigrationAutodetector.generate_altered_fields (autodetector.py): when the FK's target field was renamed (`to_field_rename_key in self.renamed_fields`), the new FK's remote_field must be repointed to BOTH the old model and the old field name: `new_field.remote_field.model = old_field.remote_field.model` (followed by `new_field.remote_field.field_name = old_field.remote_field.field_name`). ForeignKey.deconstruct() only includes `to_field` by comparing remote_field.field_name with remote_field.model's pk name, so repointing only field_name left a stale `to_field='field_wrong'` and produced a bogus AlterField after the RenameField; repointing the model too makes old/new deconstruct identically.

translation.E004 is only raised from check_language_settings_consistent in django/core/checks/translation.py. It validates LANGUAGE_CODE with get_supported_language_variant(settings.LANGUAGE_CODE) (line 62) instead of requiring an exact match in LANGUAGES. That function falls back from a sublanguage such as de-at to the base language de, so E004 is returned only when it raises LookupError (lines 63-64).

The `comments` argument is passed to `feed.add_item()` in `Feed.get_feed()` (django/contrib/syndication/views.py) via `comments=self._get_dynamic_attr("item_comments", item),`. This lets a Feed subclass define `item_comments` (attribute or method) directly, without going through `item_extra_kwargs`. `SyndicationFeed.add_item()` in django/utils/feedgenerator.py already accepts `comments=None` (line 110) and stores it (line 140), and the RSS writer emits the `<comments>` element (lines 307-308).

The bug is in SQLCompiler.find_ordering_name (django/db/models/sql/compiler.py). Child inherits Meta.ordering = ["-pk"] from Parent, and "pk" on Child resolves to the parent_ptr OneToOneField, so field.is_relation is true and opts becomes Parent._meta (which has ordering ["-pk"]). Without a guard, the "append the related model's default ordering" branch recursed with find_ordering_name("-pk", ..., default_order=order), where order was already "DESC". The inner "-pk" then flips DESC to ASC, giving ORDER BY ... ASC. The fix is the `and name != "pk"` condition, which excludes the pk shortcut from that relation branch so "-pk" goes straight to OrderBy(..., descending=True). This corpus already contains the guard, so I traced the code and did not reproduce the bug.

The TypeError comes from Q._combine() in django/db/models/query_utils.py, not from a missing __rand__. Q.__and__ is tried first (Q is the left operand) and _combine raises TypeError itself instead of returning NotImplemented, so Python never falls back to Exists.__rand__ (Combinable.__rand__ just raises NotImplementedError anyway). Previously the guard was `if not isinstance(other, Q): raise TypeError(other)`. The fix is that the guard must accept any conditional expression, not just Q instances: `if getattr(other, "conditional", False) is False: raise TypeError(other)`. Exists qualifies because BaseExpression.conditional is True when output_field is a BooleanField (Exists.output_field = BooleanField()). After that check, an empty Q returns other.copy(), otherwise the two are combined into a new Q. This makes & (and | / ^) commutative for Q/Exists pairs, matching Exists(...) & Q(...) which already worked via Combinable.__and__ -> Q(self) & Q(other).

The `|` operator is `Q.__or__` -> `Q._combine()`. The "cannot pickle 'dict_keys' object" error came from `_combine` calling `copy.deepcopy(...)` on the Q. That goes through `Node.__deepcopy__` (django/utils/tree.py:56), which runs `copy.deepcopy(self.children)`. Deep-copying a non-picklable child such as `dict_keys` falls back to the pickle protocol and raises the TypeError. In this snapshot it is already fixed. For `Q() | Q(x__in={}.keys())`, `self` is empty, so `_combine` takes the `if not self:` branch and returns `other.copy()` (the line submitted). The mirrored case `Q(x__in={}.keys()) | Q()` returns `self.copy()` at line 61. `copy()` is the shallow `Node.__copy__` in tree.py: it builds a new node via `create()` and reuses the same `children` list, so nothing is deep-copied or pickled. `query_utils.py` no longer imports `copy`. Combining non-empty Qs goes through `self.create(connector=conn)` plus `add()`, which only extends or appends children and never deep-copies them. `copy.deepcopy(Q(x__in={}.keys()))` would still raise, but nothing on the `|` path calls it now.

BoundWidget.id_for_label no longer rebuilds 'id_%s_%s' from name/index. It returns the id that ChoiceWidget.options/create_option already put in the subwidget's attrs: `return self.data["attrs"].get("id")`. That id comes from BoundField.subwidgets (widget.attrs['id'] or auto_id), so a custom auto_id format is honoured for CheckboxSelectMultiple and RadioSelect labels.

The issue's `self.validate_name(os.path.basename(target), 'directory')` no longer exists as written. In TemplateCommand.handle, the directory-name check is now `self.validate_name(os.path.basename(top_dir), "directory")` (line 106). `top_dir` is built on line 104 as `os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(target))`. abspath normalizes the path and drops the trailing slash, so `apps/app1/` becomes `/cwd/apps/app1` and basename returns `app1` instead of `''`. That avoids the "'' is not a valid app directory" error raised by validate_name (line 260). I did not execute the command to confirm.

ReadOnlyPasswordHashWidget overrides Widget.id_for_label() to return None (instead of the default, which returns the field id). BoundField.label_tag() (forms/boundfield.py:190-192) only adds a `for` attribute when widget.id_for_label(id_) is truthy. So the admin label for the read-only password hash (UserChangeForm.password) no longer gets a `for` pointing at a non-labelable element.

The extension point is the new `AutocompleteJsonView.serialize_result(self, obj, to_field_name)` method in django/contrib/admin/views/autocomplete.py. It returns `{"id": str(getattr(obj, to_field_name)), "text": str(obj)}`. `get()` now calls `self.serialize_result(obj, to_field_name)` for each object in the results list instead of building the dict inline. Subclasses can override just this method (e.g. `super().serialize_result(obj, to_field_name) | {"notes": obj.notes}`) to add extra fields without overriding `get()`.

The bug is in TypeSerializer.serialize's special case for models.Model, which writes the string "models.Model" into the migration. That case must also report the import "from django.db import models". With an empty import list, a CreateModel whose bases are (MyMixin, models.Model) gets `import app.models` and `from django.db import migrations` but no `models` import, hence the NameError. The line is `(models.Model, "models.Model", ["from django.db import models"]),`. MigrationWriter.as_string (writer.py:172-176) then merges that import into `from django.db import migrations, models`.

RenameModel.database_forwards (django/db/migrations/operations/models.py) has no early return when old_model._meta.db_table == new_model._meta.db_table. Only the schema_editor.alter_db_table() call is a noop in that case (base/schema.py:644 returns early when the names are equal). The method then still runs the "Alter the fields pointing to us" loop (schema_editor.alter_field, which drops and recreates FK constraints on Postgres and remakes the table on SQLite) and the M2M rename via _alter_many_to_many. The fix is to compute old_db_table/new_db_table right after old_model is fetched and `return` if they are equal, before the "Move the main table" alter_db_table call at line 440.

Root cause / fix: Expressions.rename_table_references() in django/db/backends/ddl_references.py. During SQLite's _remake_table(), the deferred CREATE UNIQUE INDEX Statement (built from alias-less columns, Query(alias_cols=False)) has rename_table_references() applied by alter_db_table(). The old code forced `col.alias = new_table` onto every column, producing `"new__table"."col"` inside the index expression, which SQLite rejects ('the "." operator prohibited in index expressions'). The fix is to relabel via `self.expressions.relabeled_clone({old_table: new_table})`, and Col.relabeled_clone() (expressions.py:1156-1158) returns self when alias is None, so alias-less columns stay unqualified.

The password-reset link is built in UserChangeForm.__init__ (django/contrib/auth/forms.py). The old code formatted the help text with the relative "../password/", which resolves to .../user/<to_field value>/password/ when the change page is opened via ?_to_field=uuid. The admin's "<id>/password/" route looks the user up by primary key, so that URL returns a 404. The code now formats it with f"../../{self.instance.pk}/password/" (line 190), which always points at .../user/<pk>/password/ whether the change page was reached by pk or by a to_field value.

The crash is handled in Query._get_only_select_mask (django/db/models/sql/query.py). The old `opts = cur_model._meta` code from deferred_to_data() no longer exists. The related model's mask is now built from the concrete model via `related_model = field.remote_field.model._meta.concrete_model`, so the proxy model's pk (and requested fields) are included in the select mask. Without that, the related pk is missing from the SELECT and RelatedPopulator raises "ValueError: 'id' is not in list".

The place to special-case this is the `ManagementForm` class in django/forms/formsets.py. The usual fix is to give that class its own `template_name = "django/forms/div.html"` instead of letting it inherit the form default, which was `default.html` and triggered the warning. Its output is only hidden inputs, so the template doesn't matter.

In this snapshot the `default.html` warning code is already gone. `BaseForm.template_name` now returns `self.renderer.form_template_name` (forms.py:220), and the renderer sets that to "django/forms/div.html" (renderers.py:20). `ManagementForm` has no `template_name` of its own. I ran out of tool calls before reading forms.py in full, so I haven't checked the fix against the surrounding `BaseForm` code.

The squash/optimizer fix is in CreateModel.reduce() in django/db/migrations/operations/models.py. The branch `elif isinstance(operation, RenameIndex) and operation.old_fields:` handles the index_together -> indexes transition. A RenameIndex with old_fields is what the autodetector emits for that transition. The branch removes the matching old_fields tuple from the CreateModel's `index_together` option, and drops the option if it is empty. It adds `models.Index(fields=operation.old_fields, name=operation.new_name)` to `indexes`. It returns one CreateModel with no `index_together`, so the squashed migration no longer emits the index_together deprecation warning. Related branches: AddIndex.reduce (line 932) folds a RenameIndex into the AddIndex, and RenameIndex.reduce (line 1112) chains an old_fields rename with a later rename by name.

The place where returning_fields used to be dropped is QuerySet._batched_insert. It now discriminates on the conflict mode: `if bulk_return and (on_conflict is None or on_conflict == OnConflict.UPDATE):` keeps returning_fields=self.model._meta.db_returning_fields (and passes on_conflict/update_fields/unique_fields through to _insert) for update_conflicts, so the INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE gets a RETURNING clause and the PKs are set on the objects (on backends with can_return_rows_from_bulk_insert). ignore_conflicts (OnConflict.IGNORE) still falls to the else branch with no returning_fields.
